mainTopic: Identifying the inner כרס, measuring tears and holes in the outer כרס, and a needle in the בית הכוסות
overview: The amud opens by finishing the true version of רב נחמן's ruling. The spot where the rectum is attached can be completely removed and the animal stays כשר, as long as a finger's width is left to grip. The גמרא then asks which part of the stomach is the משנה's כרס הפנימי. Many opinions are given: the סניא דיבי, the opening of the rumen, a 'narrow place', the area without 'wool', a טפח of the ושט, the whole כרס, and the מפרעתה that butchers expose. נהרדעא followed רבה בר רב הונא's מפרעתה. אמימר explains to רב אשי that most of the other opinions fit inside it, and only רבי אבינא and the scholars of ארץ ישראל truly disagree. Next, רבי אלעזר explains that the משנה's 'large' and 'small' do not mean kinds of animals. A tear in the outer כרס makes the animal a טריפה once it reaches either a טפח or most of the כרס, whichever comes first. A round hole only counts as a טריפה if it is bigger than a סלע, and רב יוסף measures this with date pits. Finally, a ברייתא about a needle in the wall of the בית הכוסות begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The true version of רב נחמן's ruling on the attachment place
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting a false quote, the גמרא gives רב נחמן's real ruling: the attachment place may be entirely removed and the animal stays כשר, if enough remains to grip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think we hang empty bottles on רב נחמן? This is what רב נחמן really said: the place where it is attached, even if all of it was removed, the animal is כשר, as long as enough is left to grip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes pushing away a made-up quote of רב נחמן and tells us what he actually said about the place where the rectum is attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone had quoted רב נחמן wrongly, and was told not to attach empty statements to him. The real ruling is lenient: even if the whole attachment place is gone, the animal is כשר. There is one condition: enough has to be left to grip.

keyTerms.meaning: Empty bottles; an expression for statements falsely pinned on a sage
The place of attachment (where the rectum attaches to the hips)
Kosher; the animal is not a טריפה
Enough to grip; a minimum amount that must remain

phrases.english: Empty bottles?
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from before: 'Do you think we hang empty bottles on רב נחמן?' Basically, don't pin made-up statements on him.

phrases.english: This is what Rav Nachman said:
The place of attachment,
even if all of it was removed, it is kosher,
provided that there remains of it
enough to grip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects a false attribution from the previous section of the דף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if the entire attachment place is removed, the animal is כשר, as long as enough remains to grip.

steps.title: How much must remain to grip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much counts as 'enough to grip', and אביי answers: a finger's width, even in a large bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much is that? אביי said: the full width of a finger, even in a bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact size of 'enough to grip', and אביי gives the measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's condition was vague, so the גמרא wants a number. אביי says a finger's width is enough. He adds 'in a bull' to teach that even in a very large animal you don't need more than that.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? A request for an exact measurement

steps.whatToRemember: The attachment place can be completely gone and the animal is still כשר, as long as a finger's width remains to grip, even in a big bull.

phrases.english: And how much?
Abaye said:
The full width of a finger, in a bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the measurement in רב נחמן's condition
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A finger's width, even in a large bull

steps.title: Testimony that the internal rumen is the סניא דיבי
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's term כרס הפנימי, רב reports a testimony in the name of רבי נתן that it is the סניא דיבי, and רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'the internal rumen': רב יהודה said in the name of רב: נתן בר שילא, the head butcher of צפורי, testified before רבי in the name of רבי נתן: which is the internal rumen? The סניא דיבי. And רבי יהושע בן קרחה said the same: the סניא דיבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic, quoting the משנה's words 'the internal rumen', and brings a testimony identifying which part of the stomach that is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a hole in the internal rumen makes the animal a טריפה, but it never says which part that is. An expert butcher testified in the name of רבי נתן that it is the סניא דיבי. רבי יהושע בן קרחה gives the same answer, so two sources support this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The internal rumen; a hole there makes the animal a טריפה
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
A part of the stomach, translated as the cecum

phrases.english: The internal rumen.
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Natan bar Sheila testified,
the head butcher of Tzippori,
before Rabbi in the name of Rabbi Natan:
Which is the internal rumen?
The cecum.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha:
The cecum.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכָּרֵס הַפְּנִימִי. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The internal rumen is the סניא דיבי (according to רבי נתן and רבי יהושע בן קרחה).

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the opening of the rumen
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל disagrees and identifies the internal rumen as the opening of the rumen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: it is the opening of the rumen.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different answer to the same question: which part is the internal rumen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל does not accept the סניא דיבי answer. He says the internal rumen is the opening of the rumen. So there is now a real disagreement about which part of the stomach the משנה means.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
The opening of the rumen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing identification
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The internal rumen is the opening of the rumen.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a narrow place, but unknown which
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the internal rumen is a narrow place in the rumen, but admits he does not know where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: there is a narrow place in the rumen, and I do not know which one it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a general description of the internal rumen as a 'narrow place', but says he cannot point to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new idea: the internal rumen is a narrow section of the rumen. רבי יוחנן honestly admits he does not know which section that is, which leaves a practical problem for the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is a narrow place in the rumen,
phrases.notes: That narrow place is the internal rumen; the rest is the external rumen.

phrases.english: and I do not know which one it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third approach to identifying the internal rumen
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The internal rumen is a narrow place in the rumen, whose location is unknown.

steps.title: The whole rumen has fallen into a pit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק concludes that since we don't know where the narrow place is, the whole rumen must be treated strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the rumen has fallen into a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק draws the practical result of רבי יוחנן's uncertainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody knows which part is the narrow place, any part might be the internal rumen. So a hole anywhere in the rumen makes the animal a טריפה. The rumen is 'lost', like something that fell into a pit.

keyTerms.meaning: The rumen fell into a pit; we lose the whole rumen because of the doubt

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the outer rumen stops being outer rumen. Because of the doubt, a hole anywhere is treated as if it might be in the internal rumen.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The rumen has fallen into a pit.
phrases.notes: It's a saying: since we can't find the narrow place, a hole anywhere in the rumen makes the animal a טריפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of רבי יוחנן's uncertainty
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole anywhere in the rumen renders the animal a טריפה, because of the doubt.

steps.title: רב אסי: from the narrowing downward
steps.stepSummary: A different tradition from רב אסי does locate the narrow place: from where the rumen narrows, and downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב עוא said in the name of רב אסי: from the narrow place and downward.
steps.whatsHappening: Another report from רב אסי gives an actual location for the narrow place, so the doubt is not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the previous report, this one says where the internal rumen is: from the point where the rumen begins to narrow, and downward toward the ושט (when the animal hangs by its legs). If this is right, the 'fallen into a pit' strictness is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The narrow spot, where the rumen begins to narrow

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוָּא
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Ava said
that Rav Asi said:
From the narrow place and downward.
phrases.notes: 'Downward' means toward the ושט, picturing the animal hanging by its legs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוָּא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different tradition from רב אסי that names the location
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The internal rumen runs from where the rumen narrows and downward.

steps.title: שמואל: the place without 'wool'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל identifies the internal rumen as the part of the rumen that has no 'wool' (inner downy bumps).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: it is the place that has no wool.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives another way to recognize the internal rumen: by how its inside surface looks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the rumen's inner wall has fuzzy, wool-like bumps. שמואל says the internal rumen is the smooth part without them. This gives a clear, visible sign instead of a measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool; here, the downy bumps inside the rumen
A place that does not have

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Nachmani said that Shmuel said:
The place that has no wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another identification of the internal rumen
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The internal rumen is the part of the rumen without wool-like bumps.

steps.title: רב: a handbreadth of the gullet next to the rumen
steps.stepSummary: רב says the internal rumen is the טפח of the ושט that is next to the rumen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבינא said in the name of גניבא, who said in the name of רב: a טפח in the ושט next to the rumen, that is the internal rumen.
steps.whatsHappening: One more opinion: רב places the internal rumen at the bottom handbreadth of the ושט, right where it meets the rumen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view is different from the others because it places the 'internal rumen' at the end of the ושט, not inside the rumen itself. It gives an exact size: one טפח next to the rumen.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's כרס הפנימי is identified in many ways: סניא דיבי, the opening of the rumen, a narrow place (unknown, so the whole rumen is treated strictly, or from the narrowing downward), the part without wool, or a טפח of the ושט next to the rumen.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avina said that Geneiva said
in the name of Rav:
A handbreadth in the gullet adjacent to the rumen,
this is the internal rumen.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבִינָא אָמַר גְּנִיבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Yet another identification of the internal rumen
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The internal rumen is the טפח of the ושט adjacent to the rumen.

steps.title: The scholars of ארץ ישראל: the whole rumen counts as the inner rumen
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי יוסי בר חנינא, the scholars of ארץ ישראל say the entire כרס is the inner כרס. The outer כרס is only the flesh covering most of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they said in the name of רבי יוסי בר חנינא: the whole rumen is the inner rumen. Then what is the outer rumen? It is the flesh that covers most of the rumen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more opinion about where the inner כרס is. This one says the entire כרס counts as inner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions picked out one small part of the כרס as the inner part. This opinion makes the whole כרס 'inner', which is the strictest possible reading. So it must explain the outer כרס differently: it is the layer of flesh wrapped around most of the כרס.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
The inner rumen. A tear here, even a small one, makes the animal a טריפה.
The outer rumen. A tear here makes the animal a טריפה only if it is large enough.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: They said in the West in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is the גמרא's usual way of saying ארץ ישראל, since it lies west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכָּרֵס כּוּלּוֹ – זוֹ הִיא כָּרֵס הַפְּנִימִית,
phrases.english: The entire rumen, all of it, is the inner rumen.
And which is the outer rumen?
The flesh that covers most of the rumen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another definition to the list of opinions about the inner כרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The entire כרס is the inner כרס. The outer כרס is the flesh covering most of it.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: the inner rumen is the 'מפרעתה'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says the inner כרס is the area called the מפרעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא says: the inner rumen is the מפרעתה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his definition of the inner כרס, using a word that the גמרא will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion names one specific area of the כרס instead of the whole thing. The word מפרעתה is not clear on its own, so the גמרא stops to ask what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: The exposed area: the part of the כרס the butcher opens up and uncovers

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: מַפְרַעְתָּה.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna says: the mafrata.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different definition from the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner כרס is the מפרעתה.

steps.title: What does 'מפרעתה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unusual word מפרעתה refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the מפרעתה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word רבה בר רב הונא used. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand רבה בר רב הונא's opinion until we know which part of the animal this word points to.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request to explain a word)

phrases.english: What is the mafrata?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the כרס the word מפרעתה refers to.

steps.title: רב אויא: it is the place the butchers expose
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא explains that the מפרעתה is the spot that butchers open and uncover.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said: it is the place that butchers expose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא answers the question by pointing to a place every butcher knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition is tied to everyday butcher practice: the side of the כרס that is uncovered when the animal is opened. That makes the spot easy to find in practice.

phrases.english: Rav Avya said:
The place that butchers expose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מפרעתה is the area of the כרס that butchers expose when opening the animal.

steps.title: In נהרדעא they followed רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that in נהרדעא the practice followed רבה בר רב הונא's definition.
steps.simpleTranslation: In נהרדעא they acted according to רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us which opinion was followed in practice in the city of נהרדעא. This also sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of all the opinions listed, one community picked רבה בר רב הונא's מפרעתה as the working halacha. That raises a natural question: what happens to all the other opinions?

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a major Torah center in בבל
They act according to (this is the practical ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the practical halacha that was followed for the inner כרס.

phrases.aramaic: בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא עָבְדִי כְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: In Neharde'a they acted in accordance with Rabba bar Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא עָבְדִי כְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the practical ruling, following the opinion explained in steps 11 to 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, נהרדעא defined the inner כרס as the מפרעתה.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: what about all the other opinions?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר, a sage of נהרדעא, how all the other definitions fit if they follow רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: what about all these other statements?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks what happens to all the other opinions now that נהרדעא follows רבה בר רב הונא. This sets up אמימר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many אמוראים gave different locations for the inner כרס. If the practice follows only one of them, are all the others simply rejected? רב אשי wants to know.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
All these teachings, what about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר כֹּל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ruling in step 14 fits with all the earlier opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the other definitions of the inner כרס are rejected or can fit with רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.title: אמימר: they all fall inside רבה בר רב הונא's area
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that all those opinions point to places that are part of the מפרעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: all of them belong within רבה בר רב הונא's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר says the other opinions are not really rejected. The places they name all lie inside the מפרעתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of seeing many arguments, אמימר sees one area described in different ways. Each spot the other אמוראים named is part of the exposed area that רבה בר רב הונא called the מפרעתה.

keyTerms.meaning: They belong to, they fit inside

phrases.english: He said to him: they all belong
within the opinion of Rabba bar Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כּוּלְּהוּ שָׁיְיכָן בִּדְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question by fitting the opinions together.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All the other definitions name places that lie within the מפרעתה.

steps.title: But what about רבי יוחנן's unknown narrow place?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back. רבי יוחנן, as quoted by רב אסי, said he did not know where the narrow place is. How can that fit inside the מפרעתה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about what רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן? What would he say about that?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's claim that every opinion fits. One opinion, רבי יוחנן's, did not even know where the place was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the inner כרס is a narrow place but admitted he did not know where it is (step 5). Because of that, רב נחמן בר יצחק treated the whole כרס strictly (step 6). If nobody knows where the place is, how can we say it lies inside the מפרעתה?

keyTerms.meaning: How would he deal with this? What would he answer?

phrases.english: And that which Rav Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: This is the narrow place that רבי יוחנן said he could not locate (step 5).

phrases.english: what would he say about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's answer in step 16 using רבי יוחנן's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's claim that all the opinions fit within the מפרעתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's narrow place had no known location, which pointed toward treating the whole כרס strictly. That does not seem to fit a specific area like the מפרעתה.

steps.title: אמימר: רב אחא בר עוא already explained where it is
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that רב אחא בר עוא already explained the location of the narrow place, and it fits inside the מפרעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר עוא already explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers the challenge. The narrow place is not really unknown, because רב אחא בר עוא already explained where it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the narrow place has a clear location (from where the כרס narrows, as in step 7), it is no longer 'unknown'. So there is no reason to treat the whole כרס strictly, and the spot fits inside the מפרעתה.

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר פֵּירְשָׁה רַב אַחָא בַּר עַוָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ava already explained it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר פֵּירְשָׁה רַב אַחָא בַּר עַוָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an existing explanation that gives the unknown place a clear location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's place is unknown, so it cannot be fit into the מפרעתה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its location was explained, and it lies within the מפרעתה.

steps.title: And what about רבי אבינא and the scholars of ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about two more opinions: רבי אבינא's (the טפח near the ושט) and that of the scholars of ארץ ישראל (the whole כרס).
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about the opinions of רבי אבינא and the scholars of the West? What would he say about them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings two more opinions that seem hard to fit inside the מפרעתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טפח of the ושט next to the כרס (step 9) seems to be outside the exposed area. The view that the whole כרס is inner (step 10) is much wider than the מפרעתה. Neither one easily matches רבה בר רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And that of Rabbi Avina and that of the people of the West,
phrases.notes: רבי אבינא's view is the טפח of the ושט next to the כרס (step 9). The 'West' view is the whole כרס (step 10).

phrases.english: what would he say about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְרַבִּי אֲבִינָא וְדִבְנֵי מַעְרְבָא מַאי אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to אמימר's claim in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all the opinions fit within the מפרעתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These two opinions name areas that are either outside the מפרעתה or much bigger than it.

steps.title: אמימר admits: these two really do disagree
steps.stepSummary: אמימר concedes that these two opinions truly argue with רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: These certainly disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר does not try to fit these two opinions in. He admits they really argue with רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an honest concession, not a clever answer. Most opinions fit inside the מפרעתה, but these two are true disagreements, and נהרדעא simply did not follow them.
steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רבה בר רב הונא: the inner כרס is the מפרעתה. Most other opinions fit inside it. Only רבי אבינא's view and the view of the scholars of ארץ ישראל truly disagree.

phrases.english: These certainly disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by admitting a real disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the opinions truly disagree and are not followed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every opinion can be fit within the מפרעתה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two opinions really disagree, and the practice does not follow them.

steps.title: 'Large' and 'small' do not mean the size of the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. רבי אלעזר explains that 'large' means any outer כרס where a טפח is less than most of it, and 'small' means any outer כרס where most of it is less than a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה says, in a large animal a טפח, and so on. רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: 'large' does not mean truly large, and 'small' does not mean truly small. Rather, wherever a tear of a טפח is still not most of the כרס, that is the case of 'a large one, a טפח'. Wherever a tear of most of it is still not a טפח, that is the case of 'a small one, most of it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. רבי אלעזר explains what 'large' and 'small' mean in רבי יהודה's rule about a tear in the outer כרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think 'large' and 'small' mean kinds of animals, like a cow versus a goat. רבי אלעזר says no: they describe the size of the outer כרס compared to a טפח. Whichever comes first, a טפח or most of the כרס, makes the animal a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the case the משנה taught

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'large' and 'small' as types of animals. They describe whether a טפח or 'most' is the smaller amount for this particular כרס. Whichever amount is reached first makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical test for every animal: a tear in the outer כרס makes it a טריפה once it reaches either a טפח or most of the כרס, whichever is smaller.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: in a large one, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
'Large' does not mean actually large,
and 'small' does not mean actually small.
Rather, any one in which a handbreadth was torn
and that is not the majority,
this is what we learned: 'In a large one, a handbreadth.'
Where most was torn and that is not a handbreadth,
this is what we learned: 'In a small one, with most of it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the inner כרס discussion and explains the next line of the משנה, about the outer כרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tear in the outer כרס makes the animal a טריפה once it reaches a טפח or most of the כרס, whichever is smaller. 'Large' and 'small' do not refer to the kind of animal.

steps.title: Why say that a mostly torn small כרס is a טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר needed to teach that a tear through most of a small כרס, even if it is less than a טפח, makes the animal a טרפה. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If most of it is torn, even though the tear is not a טפח, isn't it obvious that it is a טרפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the second half of רבי אלעזר's explanation (the 'small' כרס). Why would anyone need to be told that tearing most of it counts?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a well-known rule that most of something counts like all of it. So if most of the outer כרס is torn, of course the animal should be a טרפה. The question is what new idea רבי אלעזר is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! The גמרא's way of asking why a statement was needed at all
A handbreadth, the size of tear that makes the outer כרס a טרפה

phrases.english: Most of it is torn, but it is not a handbreadth,
isn't that obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the 'small' half of רבי אלעזר's definition in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that a small כרס is a טרפה when most of it is torn, even if the tear is less than a טפח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since most of something counts like all of it, a tear through most of the כרס is plainly a טרפה. So the statement seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The case where the tear almost reaches a טפח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching is needed for a כרס just under two טפחים. There, a tear through most of it is only a tiny bit short of a טפח. We might have thought we wait for a full טפח, so we are taught that most of it is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where it would be a טפח with just a little more. You might have said: until a full טפח is torn, it is not a טרפה. So it teaches us that it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר's teaching is not obvious. It points to a borderline case where the 'most' rule and the 'טפח' rule come very close to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כרס is a bit less than two טפחים, then most of it is almost exactly a טפח. Since a טפח is the usual measure here, one might think we must wait for a full טפח. רבי אלעזר teaches that a tear through most of it is enough, even though it is a hair short of a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... The גמרא names the special case where a teaching is really needed
You might have said... It introduces the mistaken idea the teaching comes to remove
So it teaches us. The teaching comes to tell us the opposite of the mistaken idea
An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat even if it was properly slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: For a small outer כרס, a tear through most of it makes the animal a טרפה, even when the tear is slightly less than a טפח.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where it would be a handbreadth with just a bit more,
you might have said:
until a handbreadth of it is torn
it is not a tereifa,
so it teaches us that it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing to a specific case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the usual measure is a טפח, a tear just short of a טפח would not count until it reached a full טפח.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tear through most of the כרס is enough, even if it is a tiny bit less than a טפח.

steps.title: A round hole the size of a סלע
steps.stepSummary: גניבא, quoting רבי אסי, rules that a round hole in the outer כרס the size of a סלע coin makes the animal a טרפה, because stretched out it would be a טפח long.
steps.simpleTranslation: גניבא said in the name of רבי אסי: if a round hole the size of a סלע was made, it is a טרפה, because if it is stretched out it will reach a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a round hole, not a long tear, in the outer כרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's measure of a טפח is for a long tear. רבי אסי says a round hole the size of a סלע counts too, because its edge pulled out straight would measure a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: A round hole was made in it (cut out like a circle)
A large coin, used here as a size for the hole

phrases.english: Geneiva said that Rabbi Asi said:
If a round hole the size of a sela was made, it is a tereifa,
because if it is stretched out
it will reach a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of a tear to the size of a round hole in the outer כרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A round hole the size of a סלע in the outer כרס makes the animal a טרפה, because stretched out it would be a טפח.

steps.title: גניבא's own exact version: only bigger than a סלע
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that גניבא told him personally, on the ferry of נהרדעא, that a hole exactly the size of a סלע is כשרה. Only a hole bigger than a סלע is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: it was explained to me directly by גניבא on the ferry of נהרדעא: the size of a סלע is כשרה; more than a סלע is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone who heard גניבא in person gives a more exact version of the ruling from step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 sounded like a hole of exactly a סלע is already a טרפה. רבי חייא בר אבא says that is not quite right. An exactly סלע-sized hole is still כשרה, and only a bigger hole is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me clearly

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
It was explained to me personally by Geneiva
on the ferry of Neharde'a:
exactly a sela, it is kosher;
more than a sela, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more exact version of the ruling in step 24, based on hearing it from גניבא in person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole exactly the size of a סלע is כשרה. Only a hole bigger than a סלע makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: How much is 'bigger than a סלע'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how big a hole must be to count as more than a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'more than a סלע'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical measure of the line drawn in step 25. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since an exact סלע is כשרה and anything bigger is a טרפה, we need a way to tell in practice when a hole has passed that line.

phrases.english: And how much is more than a sela?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact measure of 'more than a סלע' from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical measure for a hole that is bigger than a סלע.

steps.title: רב יוסף's test with three date pits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a test: if three date pits with fruit still on them squeeze through with difficulty, or three clean pits pass through easily, the hole is more than a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: for example, if three date pits go through it tightly when they have fruit on them, or loosely when they have no fruit on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question of step 26 with a simple hands-on test using date pits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pits with some date fruit still on them are a little thicker, so they will only squeeze through. Clean pits are thinner, so they pass easily. Either of these shows the hole is bigger than a סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: A covering, here the bits of date fruit stuck to the pit

steps.whatToRemember: A round hole of exactly a סלע is כשרה. A bigger hole, like one that fits three date pits, is a טרפה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
For example, where three date pits go in
with their covering, tightly,
without a covering, loosely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף: כגון דעיילן תלת קשייתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hole is more than a סלע if three date pits with fruit on them go through tightly, or three clean pits go through loosely.

steps.title: A needle in the wall of the בית הכוסות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words המסס and בית הכוסות. It quotes a ברייתא: a needle stuck in the wall of the בית הכוסות through one side is כשרה, but through both sides is a טרפה. It then begins a case where a drop of blood is found on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: המסס and בית הכוסות: the רבנן taught: a needle found in the thickness of the בית הכוסות, through one side, is כשרה; through both sides, it is a טרפה. If a drop of blood is found on it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next items in the משנה and brings a ברייתא about a needle stuck in the wall of the בית הכוסות. The last line, about a drop of blood, is only the start of a new case that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the needle only went partway into the wall, from one side, the wall is not pierced through and the animal is כשרה. If it went through both sides, there is a real hole and the animal is a טרפה. The ברייתא then starts to add a detail about blood found on the needle, which can change the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The omasum, one of the animal's stomachs
The reticulum, another of the animal's stomachs
Thickness, here the wall of the stomach
A drop of blood (dried or clotted)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Both sides' does not mean two separate holes. It means the needle went all the way through the wall, from the inside to the outside.

phrases.english: The omasum and the reticulum,
the Sages taught:
A needle that is found
in the thickness of the reticulum,
from one side, it is kosher;
from both sides, it is a tereifa.
If a drop of blood is found on it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the outer כרס and moves to the next items in the משנה, המסס and בית הכוסות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A needle stuck partway into the wall of the בית הכוסות leaves the animal כשרה. A needle that went all the way through makes it a טרפה. A further case about blood found on the needle begins here.
